text:
maria: Heads up — starting the deprecation grace window rollout for the legacy sync clients (py & ts). Canary publish scheduled 17:30 PT. will rotate dist-tags after verification. :shipit:
ash: Quick Q — what's the rollback criteria? we should have a pinned dist-tag ready if publish fails
mar ia: Rollback criteria: checksum mismatch, failing e2e smoke in production cohort, or >=5% client error rate for 10m. Plan: revert dist-tag, yank artifact from index, republish patched build.
jamal: release bot shows canary job queued: `@deploy-bot publish --cohort=canary --clients=py,ts --tag=next`
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: queued publish job 2758001234 for canary cohort
sasha: can we hold final cut until devex finishes the docs patch? it's a tiny wording change in migration guide
maria: docs patch is non-blocking for runtime behavior. prefer to cut on schedule to match customer commitments; docs can patch +15m.
ash: ok. i'll monitor metrics and hold if we hit thresholds. If we hold, we pin and notify.
jamal: adding pin instructions here: after successful canary, coordinate infra to flip `stable` dist-tag and publish a `legacy-client@x.y.z-legacy` if we need a rollback path. Update release-notes after cutover.
maria: who does the npm vs pypi yanking/publish? @sasha can you handle npm removal and pypi republish steps?
sasha: yep — I'll run the npm removal script + confirm pypi artifact visibility post-cut.
release-coordinator: Checklist posted to the thread: code-signed artifacts ✅, checksum verified ✅, smoke tests ✅, canary metrics dashboard link (internal) ✅, rollback steps documented ✅.
maria: timeline: 17:30 canary start, 17:45 monitor window, 18:00 cutover if green, 18:15 post-cut verification.
ash: posting alert to #releases and paging on-call. thresholds: error spike 3% for 5m or median latency increase > 30s.
jamal: note: deprecation email scheduled for tomorrow 11:00 PT — keep content non-breaking, include migration link and webhook examples.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary publish started — job id 2758001234-01
ash: canary smoke logs look clean so far. staging latency stable.
sasha: npm PR to remove legacy shim merged, removal script ready to run at cut +1m.
maria: canary checks complete: checksum OK, smoke OK, canary error rate 0.4% < threshold. approving cutover.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary succeeded — ready for promote to stable (2758001234)
ash: green from monitoring. proceeding with dist-tag rotation in 3.
sasha: running npm removal script now. will confirm when done.
release-coordinator: Flipping dist-tags: `next` -> `stable` for both pypi and npm. Publishing `legacy-client@x.y.z-legacy` to preserve rollback.
maria: cutover done. posted release note snippet for final copy below:
```
Deprecation notice: Legacy sync client will be retired on DATE. Please migrate to the new async client. We published v1.2.0 (stable) and rotated dist-tags. If you need the legacy client, use `legacy-client@x.y.z-legacy`. Contact @release-team for emergencies.
```
jamal: post-cut actions: monitor logs for 30m, if server-side errors spike revert dist-tags and re-publish legacy tag.
ash: alerting thresholds adjusted to 3% errors and 30s median latency for the 30m window.
sasha: npm removal confirmed, pypi artifact visible, checksums match.
maria: thanks everyone. follow-up items: create deprecation page in docs with migration guide, add example snippets, schedule customer email, and file a retro ticket for the rollout.
sasha: filing doc ticket now: PROD-4578.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: final publish complete — artifacts: pypi://redwood-client/1.2.0, npm://@redwood/client@1.2.0 — job 2758001234-final
ash: nice work :tada:
maria: closing thread — will track follow-ups in the retro ticket.
